dedupe_keys.name: stormwater management to protect lake saimaa water quality in lappeenranta climate adapt case study

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes Lappeenranta's stormwater management programme, which protects drinking and bathing water quality in Lake Saimaa as heavier rain, floods and snowmelt carry more contaminants from streets. The Stormwater Management Plan, prepared in three workshops in 2019 with the local water utility, the rescue service and the regional ELY Centre, sets rules for green strips, biofiltration, permeable pavements and open ditches; a new street drainage system with sensors for remote monitoring of stormwater quality is being built, and 11 nature-based sites are planned, eight already in place. The Heinäkatu retention basin cost 132,000 euros for 3,000 m2. Coverage is the city of Lappeenranta in Finland. The page is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal, published in 2024 and updated in 2026. Caveats: structures are sized for yearly or twice-yearly rain plus a 20 per cent climate margin, some sites lack room even for that, and more structures raise maintenance needs. Simulation uses: design standards and nature-based options for urban drainage adaptation. Related records: the Rimini sewer overflow case study (case_study-rimini-psbo-sewer-overflow-bathing-water).
name: Stormwater management to protect Lake Saimaa water quality in Lappeenranta (Climate-ADAPT case study)
outcomes: Eight nature-based measures were in place when the page was written, with 11 sites planned in all, including the Koulukatu infiltration pilot of the TransformAr project.
